LocalBusiness schema generated for branch widgets with: name, address, telephone, aggregateRating (ratingValue, reviewCount, bestRating, worstRating), review array (up to 10 most recent)
Organization schema generated for company widgets with: name, url, logo, aggregateRating, review array
Person schema generated for LO widgets with: name, jobTitle, worksFor, aggregateRating
AggregateRating always includes: @type, ratingValue (to 1 decimal), reviewCount, bestRating (5), worstRating (1)
Individual Review schema includes: @type, author.name, datePublished (ISO 8601), reviewRating.ratingValue, reviewBody (truncated to 200 chars)
Schema type selectable via config.seo.schemaType: 'LocalBusiness', 'Organization', 'FinancialService', 'MortgageBroker'
Structured data validated against Google Rich Results Test requirements
/api/v1/widgets/:widgetId/structured-data endpoint returns raw JSON-LD for external consumption
Only one JSON-LD block injected per widget even if widget re-renders
JSON-LD block removed when widget is destroyed via RepWell.destroy()
Dashboard SEO tab shows live preview of generated structured data with syntax highlighting

key_decisions: JSON-LD injected into <head> outside Shadow DOM since search engines need it in main document
Shared generator function used by both embed.js client-side injection and server-side API endpoint
Review body truncated to 200 chars in schema to avoid excessively large JSON-LD blocks
MortgageBroker schema type maps to schema.org/MortgageBroker if available, fallback to FinancialService

stories.title: Domain Allowlist & CORS Enforcement
stories.description: Implement domain-level access control for widgets, ensuring widgets only render on authorized domains. Includes CORS header management, allowlist CRUD in dashboard, and embed.js client-side domain validation.
acceptance_criteria: widget_configs.allowed_domains stores array of authorized hostnames (e.g., ['example.com', 'www.example.com'])
Public API endpoints check Origin header against allowed_domains; return 403 with error message if origin not in list
Empty allowed_domains array means widget is unrestricted (renders on any domain)
CORS Access-Control-Allow-Origin set to requesting origin if in allowlist, or '*' if unrestricted
embed.js performs client-side domain check before fetching config; shows 'Widget not authorized for this domain' message if blocked
Domain allowlist editor in Widget Builder: text input with add button, removable chips for each domain, validation for valid hostname format
Wildcard subdomain support: '*.example.com' matches any subdomain of example.com
localhost and 127.0.0.1 always allowed in development (controlled by widget status=draft)
Dashboard preview always renders regardless of domain allowlist
API returns allowed_domains in config only to authenticated dashboard requests, not in public config endpoint
Rate limiting on 403 responses to prevent enumeration attacks (progressive delay after 10 failures per IP)
Unit tests cover: exact match, wildcard match, empty allowlist, blocked domain, localhost in draft mode

key_decisions: Client-side domain check in embed.js is a UX convenience, not a security boundary; server CORS is the enforcement layer
Wildcard matching uses simple string comparison (endsWith) not regex for security
allowed_domains stripped from public config response to prevent leaking authorized domains
Draft status widgets allow localhost to enable development/testing

stories.title: CDN Deployment for embed.js & Static Assets
stories.description: Configure CDN delivery for embed.js script and widget static assets (SVGs, fonts) with proper caching, versioning, and cache-busting strategies.
acceptance_criteria: embed.js served from CDN URL: https://cdn.repwell.com/embed/v1/embed.min.js (or Vercel Edge equivalent)
Script served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400, immutable for versioned files
Cache-busting via content hash in filename (embed.{hash}.min.js) with stable /v1/embed.min.js redirect
Version manifest file at /embed/v1/manifest.json listing current version, hash, and size
Static assets (Equal Housing SVG, placeholder avatar) bundled inline or served from same CDN path
Gzip and Brotli compression enabled for .js files on CDN
CDN serves correct CORS headers for cross-origin script loading (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *)
Build pipeline: TypeScript compile → esbuild bundle → hash → upload to CDN → update manifest
Rollback capability: previous versions accessible at /embed/v1/{version}/embed.min.js
CDN health check endpoint returns 200 with version info
Source maps uploaded but not publicly linked (available for error tracking)
Build script integrated into CI/CD pipeline with size gate (fails if > 15KB gzipped)

key_decisions: Use Vercel Edge Network as CDN since project already deployed on Vercel
Content-hashed filenames with stable URL redirect ensures cache invalidation on deploy while allowing long-lived caches
Source maps stored separately for error tracking services (Sentry) but not exposed publicly
Version manifest enables embed.js self-update checking (future feature)

stories.title: Widget Analytics Dashboard
stories.description: Build the dashboard analytics page for widget performance tracking, showing impressions, clicks, conversion metrics, and per-widget breakdowns with date range filtering and charts.
acceptance_criteria: Analytics page at /dashboard/widgets/analytics (or tab within /dashboard/widgets)
Summary cards at top: Total Impressions, Total Clicks, Click-Through Rate (CTR), Write Review Clicks, unique page URLs with widgets
Date range filter: Last 7 days, Last 30 days, Last 90 days, Custom range (date picker)
Line chart showing daily impressions and clicks over selected date range
Per-widget table: widget name, type icon, impressions, clicks, CTR, top referrer, status — sortable by any column
Widget detail drill-down shows: daily impression/click chart, event type breakdown (pie chart), top page URLs, top referrers, geographic breakdown (by IP hash country if available)
Events aggregated server-side via SQL queries on widget_events table, not client-side
GET /api/dashboard/widgets/:id/analytics endpoint returns aggregated data with 5min cache
Dashboard analytics server action returns aggregated metrics for all widgets in organization
Data export: CSV download of analytics table
Empty state when no widgets or no events yet, with CTA to create first widget
Loading states with skeletons for all charts and tables
Real-time impression counter updates via polling (60s interval) on widget detail page

key_decisions: Aggregation queries use date_trunc and GROUP BY for time-series, not individual event rows
CTR calculated as (click events / impression events) * 100
5min server-side cache on analytics API to reduce database load from frequent dashboard refreshes
Charts use Recharts (already in project dependencies) for consistency with existing analytics pages

stories.title: Branch Review Widget
stories.description: Implement the Branch Review Widget type that displays branch-level aggregated reviews with branch info, address, team members, and branch-specific compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Widget renders branch name, address, phone number, aggregate star rating, total review count
Optional team member grid showing LOs at the branch with headshots, names, and individual ratings
Review cards show same fields as Company Review Widget plus branch-specific LO attribution
Branch NMLS number displayed (fallback to company NMLS) with nmlsconsumeraccess.org link
Reviews filtered to branch entity_id from widget_configs
Rating distribution bar chart for branch reviews
Sort and filter controls matching Company Review Widget patterns
All 8 theme presets render correctly
Responsive: team member grid collapses to 2-col on tablet, 1-col on mobile
Events tracked: impression, click_review, click_cta, click_write_review, filter_change
Dashboard preview component with real branch data
Compliance footer with branch-level Equal Housing and disclaimer
Widget works correctly when branch has 0 reviews (shows empty state with CTA)

key_decisions: Team member grid is optional via config.content.showTeam boolean
Branch entity_id joins to branches table for address/phone data included in config API response
LO attribution on review cards links to LO's individual profile page if available

stories.title: Review Carousel Widget
stories.description: Implement the auto-rotating Review Carousel widget with slide, fade, and flip transition effects, configurable speed, navigation dots/arrows, and responsive visible card count.
acceptance_criteria: Carousel auto-plays through reviews at configurable interval (config.carousel.interval, default 5000ms)
Three transition modes: slide (translateX), fade (opacity), flip (3D rotateY) — selected via config.carousel.transition
config.carousel.visibleCards controls cards shown simultaneously (1-4, responsive breakpoints)
Navigation dots shown/hidden per config.carousel.showDots, clickable to jump to specific review
Left/right arrow buttons shown/hidden per config.carousel.showArrows
Auto-play pauses on hover and resumes on mouse leave
Auto-play pauses when widget is not visible (using Intersection Observer)
Touch/swipe support on mobile devices for manual navigation
Keyboard accessible: arrow keys navigate, Enter/Space activates dots
Smooth CSS transitions (300ms default) with requestAnimationFrame for flip effect
Infinite loop: after last review, seamlessly loops back to first
Review cards use same rendering as LO/Company/Branch review cards (shared template)
Events tracked: impression, carousel_navigate (with direction and index in metadata), click_review, click_cta
Dashboard preview shows carousel with play/pause control and transition preview

key_decisions: Carousel engine is pure vanilla JS; no carousel library to stay within bundle budget
Flip transition uses CSS perspective and backface-visibility, not canvas/WebGL
Infinite loop implemented by cloning first/last cards and resetting position after transition
Touch handling uses native touch events (touchstart, touchmove, touchend) not a gesture library

stories.title: Video Testimonial Widget
stories.description: Implement the Video Testimonial Widget with inline video player, transcript display, poster image, and video-specific analytics events.
acceptance_criteria: Widget renders video player with poster image (thumbnail), play button overlay, and LO/reviewer info
Video plays inline using native HTML5 <video> element (no third-party player library)
Custom playback controls inside Shadow DOM: play/pause, progress bar, time display, volume, fullscreen
Transcript display panel below or beside video (configurable via config.video.transcriptPosition: 'below' | 'side' | 'hidden')
Transcript auto-scrolls and highlights current segment during playback
Multiple video testimonials displayed as a scrollable list or grid (configurable)
Video lazy-loads: poster image shown initially, video source fetched only on play intent (hover or click)
Responsive: video scales to container width, controls resize for touch targets on mobile
Events tracked: impression, video_play (with video_id), video_pause, video_complete, video_progress (25%, 50%, 75%, 100%)
LO info displayed alongside video: name, headshot, NMLS, rating
Compliance disclaimer shown below video player
Fallback state for videos that fail to load: error message with retry button
Dashboard preview plays actual video with all controls functional

key_decisions: Native HTML5 video element keeps bundle small; custom controls styled via Shadow DOM CSS
Video lazy-loading: only poster loads initially,
Transcript data fetched alongside video config, stored as timed segments [{start, end, text}]
Video progress events throttled to one per milestone (25/50/75/100) per session to avoid event spam

stories.title: Review Wall Widget (Masonry Grid)
stories.description: Implement the Review Wall widget using masonry grid layout to display a visually dynamic collection of review cards with varied heights.
acceptance_criteria: Masonry grid layout where cards fill columns based on content height (no equal-height rows)
Configurable column count: 2-5 columns on desktop, responsive breakdowns for tablet (2-3) and mobile (1)
Column count configurable via config.wall.columns with responsive overrides
Review cards vary in height based on review text length (no truncation by default, optional truncation via config)
Cards include: star rating, reviewer name, review text, date, source icon, loan type tag, avatar
Optional featured/highlighted cards with visual emphasis (larger card, accent border) for featured reviews
Load more button or infinite scroll (configurable via config.wall.loadMore: 'button' | 'scroll' | 'none')
Masonry layout recalculates on window resize and new card insertion with smooth animation
CSS-only masonry using CSS columns (column-count, column-gap, break-inside: avoid) for zero-JS layout cost
Fallback to flex-wrap grid for browsers without CSS columns support
Events tracked: impression, click_review, scroll_depth (25%, 50%, 75%, 100% of wall height)
Empty state when no reviews match filters
Dashboard preview shows masonry layout with column count slider

key_decisions: CSS columns used for masonry instead of JS-calculated positions to minimize bundle size and layout thrash
Infinite scroll uses Intersection Observer on a sentinel element at bottom of wall
Featured cards use column-span: all on wide layouts for visual emphasis
Scroll depth tracking uses percentage thresholds on the widget container, not the page

stories.title: NPS Score Badge Widget
stories.description: Implement the NPS Score Badge widget showing the organization's Net Promoter Score in gauge or numeric display format with color-coded zones.
acceptance_criteria: Two display modes: gauge (semicircular dial with needle) and numeric (large number with label)
Gauge mode renders SVG semicircle with colored zones: red (0-6 Detractors), yellow (7-8 Passives), green (9-10 Promoters)
Gauge needle animates from 0 to actual NPS on first render (CSS animation, 1.5s ease-out)
Numeric mode shows NPS as large number with +/- sign, color-coded (red <0, yellow 0-30, light green 30-70, dark green 70+)
NPS score label text configurable: 'Net Promoter Score', 'NPS', or custom text
Response count displayed below score (e.g., 'Based on 456 responses')
Time period label (e.g., 'Last 12 months') based on widget filters
Optional promoter/passive/detractor percentage breakdown bar
Widget config supports display mode (gauge | numeric), showBreakdown, showCount, showPeriod
All 8 theme presets render correctly with appropriate color overrides for NPS zones
Events tracked: impression, click_cta
Dashboard preview shows both display modes with toggle
Accessible: ARIA announces 'Net Promoter Score is X based on N responses'

key_decisions: SVG gauge rendered as inline SVG string (no external library) to stay within bundle budget
NPS calculated server-side via reviews API with NPS-specific aggregation query
Gauge animation uses CSS transform: rotate() with transition, not requestAnimationFrame
Color zones are hardcoded industry-standard NPS ranges, not theme-customizable

stories.title: Social Proof Banner Widget
stories.description: Implement the Social Proof Banner widget supporting notification popups, review counters, and floating bars with trigger/frequency/dismissal logic.
acceptance_criteria: Three banner modes: notification popup (toast-style), counter bar (fixed bar with stats), floating badge (floating element with recent review)
Notification popup: shows recent reviews one at a time with reviewer name, star rating, snippet, and LO name — auto-rotates every config.banner.interval ms
Counter bar: fixed top or bottom bar showing '★ 4.8 average from 1,234 reviews' with CTA button
Floating badge: small floating element in configurable corner showing latest review with expand-on-hover
Placement configurable: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right, top-bar, bottom-bar via config.banner.placement
Trigger options: immediate, scroll (show after scrolling X%), time (show after X seconds), exit-intent (show on mouse leave viewport)
Frequency options via config.banner.frequency: every_visit, once_per_session, once_per_day, once_per_week
Frequency tracking uses localStorage with widget_id key
Dismissable: config.banner.dismissable controls whether close button is shown; dismissed state persisted per frequency setting
Enter/exit animations: slide-in from placement edge, fade, bounce — configurable
Banner z-index configurable (default: 99999) to ensure visibility over host page elements
Events tracked: impression, banner_click, banner_dismiss
Mobile-responsive: banners resize for mobile viewports, notification becomes full-width bottom toast
Dashboard preview shows all three modes with trigger simulation

key_decisions: Banner rendered outside normal Shadow DOM container — appended to document.body in its own Shadow DOM host for proper fixed positioning
localStorage used for frequency tracking; graceful fallback (show every time) if localStorage unavailable
Exit-intent detection uses mouseleave on document.documentElement with Y-position check
Trigger engine is event-driven: registers listeners on init, fires show event once trigger condition met

stories.title: Advanced Filtering (Loan Type, Keyword, Date Range)
stories.description: Implement advanced review filtering capabilities within widgets and the builder: loan type filter, keyword search, date range, source filter, and sort options — both in the public API and as interactive controls within widgets.
acceptance_criteria: Widget filter config supports: minRating (1-5), dateRange (last_30d, last_90d, last_year, all_time, custom start/end), sources (array of 'google' | 'zillow' | 'internal' | 'facebook'), maxReviews (1-100), sortOrder ('newest' | 'oldest' | 'highest' | 'lowest'), featuredOnly (boolean), keywords (string array), loanTypes (array of 'Purchase' | 'Refinance' | 'VA' | 'FHA' | 'Jumbo' | 'USDA' | 'Conventional')
Public reviews API applies all filters server-side via parameterized SQL queries
Keyword filter searches review text using PostgreSQL full-text search (ts_vector) for performance
Loan type filter joins on review metadata JSONB field where loan_type matches
Interactive filter controls optionally rendered within widget when config.content.showFilters is true
Interactive controls: rating star filter (click to filter 5-star, 4+, 3+, etc.), source dropdown, loan type pills, sort dropdown
Filter changes update widget content dynamically without page reload (fetches filtered reviews from API)
filter_change event tracked with metadata containing filter type and value
Widget Builder filter tab shows all filter options with real-time preview of matching review count
Combined filters use AND logic (all conditions must match)
Empty result state displayed when filters return no reviews: 'No reviews match your filters' with reset button
Filter state not persisted in URL or localStorage (resets on page reload for embed context)

key_decisions: Full-text search via PostgreSQL ts_vector for keyword filtering; index created on reviews.text column
Filters applied server-side to prevent data leakage (e.g., showing reviews below minRating threshold)
Interactive filter controls are shared components used across all widget types
Filter state managed within embed.js widget instance state, triggering re-fetch on change

stories.title: Widget A/B Testing Framework
stories.description: Implement A/B testing capabilities for widgets, allowing users to create variants of a widget with different configurations and measure performance differences.
acceptance_criteria: A/B test creation flow in Widget Builder: select base widget → create variant → configure differences → set traffic split → activate test
Variant widget stored as separate widget_configs row with parent_widget_id pointing to base widget and ab_test_group set ('A' or 'B')
Traffic splitting: configurable percentage (e.g., 50/50, 70/30, 80/20) stored in parent widget config
embed.js resolves A/B variant: fetches parent config, checks ab_test split, assigns visitor to group using consistent hashing on a cookie/localStorage visitor ID
Visitor assignment is sticky: same visitor always sees same variant (persisted via localStorage key per widget)
A/B test analytics view: side-by-side comparison of impressions, clicks, CTR, write review clicks for each variant
Statistical significance indicator using chi-squared test (shows 'Not enough data', '90% confident', '95% confident', '99% confident')
Declare winner action: promotes winning variant to active widget, deactivates losing variant, preserves analytics history
Only one active A/B test per base widget at a time
Test duration tracker: shows days running, events collected, estimated days to significance
A/B test list view on analytics page showing all running/completed tests
Cancel test action: reverts to base widget for all visitors

key_decisions: Consistent hashing (visitor ID + widget ID) ensures deterministic variant assignment without server roundtrip
Chi-squared test for statistical significance is standard for conversion rate comparison
Variant as separate widget_configs row simplifies API (embed.js fetches variant config just like any widget)
Parent widget config stores ab_test metadata: {enabled, splitPercent, variantWidgetId, startedAt}

stories.title: Enhanced Widget Analytics (Scroll Depth, Video, Conversion Attribution)
stories.description: Extend widget analytics with scroll depth tracking, video playback analytics, conversion attribution, and per-event-type dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Scroll depth events fired at 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% thresholds of widget container height (for Review Wall and long widgets)
Scroll depth tracked via Intersection Observer on sentinel elements placed at each threshold
Video play tracking: video_play (on start), video_pause, video_complete events with video_id in metadata
Video progress milestones: 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% watched events with duration and current time in metadata
Conversion attribution: optional config.analytics.conversionUrl pattern; when visitor navigates to matching URL after interacting with widget, conversion event recorded via redirect tracking pixel
Conversion tracking pixel: 1x1 transparent image loaded from /api/v1/widgets/:widgetId/pixel?event=conversion&session=xxx
Analytics dashboard sections: Overview (all events), Engagement (scroll depth heatmap), Video (play rate, completion rate, average watch time), Conversions (attributed conversions, conversion rate)
Scroll depth heatmap shows percentage of visitors reaching each depth threshold as horizontal bar chart
Video analytics: play rate (plays / impressions), completion rate (completes / plays), average watch duration
Conversion funnel visualization: impressions → clicks → conversions with drop-off percentages
All enhanced events stored in widget_events with appropriate event_type and metadata JSONB
Analytics data exportable as CSV with event-level granularity
Rate limiting on event ingestion: max 50 events per widget per visitor session

key_decisions: Scroll depth uses Intersection Observer on sentinel divs rather than scroll event listeners for performance
Conversion tracking uses session-based attribution (same session ID across widget interaction and conversion)
Tracking pixel approach avoids CORS issues on conversion page and works even if embed.js isn't on conversion page
Event rate limiting enforced both client-side (embed.js) and server-side (API) to prevent abuse

stories.title: @repwell/react-widgets NPM Package
stories.description: Build and publish a React component library NPM package providing all 9 widget types as React components with TypeScript types, SSR support, and tree-shaking.
acceptance_criteria: Package published as @repwell/react-widgets to NPM registry

Exports named components: <LOReviewWidget />, <BranchReviewWidget />, <CompanyReviewWidget />, <ReviewCarousel />, <StarRatingBadge />, <VideoTestimonialWidget />, <ReviewWall />, <NPSScoreBadge />, <SocialProofBanner />
Each component accepts widgetId prop (fetches config from API) OR inline config prop (for custom configuration)
Components accept optional className and style props for host-side customization
TypeScript types exported for all config schemas, props, and event callbacks
onEvent callback prop fires for all widget events (impression, click, etc.) for host app analytics integration
Server-side rendering (SSR) compatible: components render static HTML on server, hydrate on client
Tree-shakeable: importing one component does not bundle others (ESM output with sideEffects: false)
Package includes CSS module that can be imported separately or auto-injected
Bundle size per component < 10KB gzipped (measured per entry point)
README with installation instructions, usage examples for Next.js/Vite/CRA, TypeScript examples, and SSR guide
Peer dependencies: react >=18, react-dom >=18 (no other dependencies)
Automated npm publish via GitHub Actions on version tag
Unit tests for all 9 components covering render, config loading, event emission

key_decisions: Monorepo structure: packages/react-widgets within main repo using npm workspaces
Rollup for build to produce ESM + CJS bundles with CSS extraction
React components wrap the same rendering logic as embed.js but using React DOM instead of manual DOM manipulation
useWidgetConfig hook handles API fetching with SWR-like caching for React context

stories.title: WordPress Plugin (Shortcode-Based)
stories.description: Build a WordPress plugin that allows WordPress users to embed RepWell widgets via shortcodes with a visual block editor integration.
acceptance_criteria: WordPress plugin installable via zip upload or (future) WordPress.org directory
Settings page in WP Admin for entering RepWell API base URL and optional API key
Shortcode [repwell_widget id='widget_id'] renders the widget embed div and loads embed.js
Shortcode supports optional attributes: width, height, class for customization
embed.js loaded once per page regardless of number of shortcodes (deduplication logic)
Gutenberg block 'RepWell Widget' with widget_id input field and live preview in editor
Classic Editor: TinyMCE button to insert shortcode with widget ID prompt
Widget renders correctly in WordPress themes (tested with Twenty Twenty-Four, Divi, Elementor)
No conflicts with common WordPress plugins (Yoast SEO, WooCommerce, Elementor)
PHP 7.4+ compatible with WordPress 6.0+ minimum
Plugin readme.txt with installation, usage, and FAQ sections
Uninstall hook cleans up plugin options from wp_options table

key_decisions: Shortcode-based approach for maximum WordPress version compatibility
embed.js loaded from CDN, not bundled in plugin (always latest version)
Gutenberg block uses ServerSideRender for editor preview
Plugin is a thin wrapper; all rendering logic lives in embed.js

stories.title: Social Proof Editor (Drag-and-Drop Canvas)
stories.description: Build the drag-and-drop Social Proof Editor for creating custom review graphics with movable, resizable elements on a configurable canvas.
acceptance_criteria: Editor page at /dashboard/social-graphics with canvas workspace

Canvas size presets: Instagram Post (1080x1080), Instagram Story (1080x1920), Facebook Post (1200x630), LinkedIn Post (1200x627), Twitter/X Post (1600x900), Website Banner (1920x400), Email Header (600x200), Custom (user-defined width x height)

Draggable elements palette: review quote text, star rating display, reviewer name, reviewer photo, LO photo, company logo, background shapes (rectangle, circle, rounded rect), icons library, text blocks (custom text), NPS score display, stats blocks (e.g., '4.8 avg / 1234 reviews')
Elements are draggable on canvas with position snapping to grid (configurable grid size)
Elements are resizable via corner/edge handles with aspect ratio lock option
Element property panel: position (x, y), size (width, height), rotation (degrees), opacity, z-index (layer order), fill color, border, font (family, size, weight, color, alignment), padding
Layer panel showing all elements with drag-to-reorder, visibility toggle, lock toggle, and delete
Canvas supports background: solid color, gradient (linear, radial), image upload
Undo/redo support (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z) with 50-step history
Zoom controls: fit to screen, 50%, 75%, 100%, 150%, 200%
Save graphic to social_proof_graphics table with full elements JSONB
Load existing graphic for editing from social_proof_graphics table
Duplicate graphic action creates a copy with '(Copy)' suffix

key_decisions: Canvas implemented with HTML/CSS positioned elements (not <canvas>) for accessibility and easier text editing
Drag and resize uses native pointer events with transform: translate() for smooth movement
Editor state managed with useReducer + immer for immutable updates to deeply nested element trees
Undo/redo implemented as a state history stack in useHistory custom hook
Elements stored as JSON array in social_proof_graphics.elements for server-side rendering

stories.title: Template Library & Auto-Generation
stories.description: Build the template library with 8+ pre-designed social proof graphic templates, auto-generation from top reviews, batch generation, and scheduled 'Review of the Week' graphics.
acceptance_criteria: Template library accessible from Social Proof Editor with visual previews

8 templates implemented: 5-Star Review Spotlight (single review highlight), Monthly Review Roundup (top 4 reviews grid), LO Spotlight (LO photo + stats + best review), Milestone Celebration (review count milestone), NPS Score Announcement (NPS gauge + key stats), Before & After (side-by-side comparison quote), Team Excellence (team stats + top reviews), Holiday Themed (seasonal border/graphics with review)
Each template is a pre-configured elements JSONB that populates the canvas on selection
Templates adapt to selected canvas size (elements reposition proportionally)
Auto-generation: 'Generate from Review' action selects a review and populates the best-matching template
Auto-generation pulls reviewer name, rating, review text, LO info, dates from selected review
Batch generation: select multiple reviews → select template → generate one graphic per review → save all to social_proof_graphics
Scheduled generation: configure 'Review of the Week' to auto-generate a graphic from the highest-rated review each week
Schedule stored in social_proof_graphics.schedule_cron, executed via cron job API route
Scheduled graphics use a designated template and auto-select the top review from the past week not previously featured
Template customization: user can edit any template after applying it (it just pre-populates the canvas)
Template thumbnails generated and cached for fast browsing
API route POST /api/dashboard/social-graphics/generate handles auto and batch generation

key_decisions: Templates are TypeScript functions that take canvas size + review data and return elements array
Proportional repositioning uses percentage-based coordinates converted to absolute at render time
Scheduled generation uses Vercel Cron (or similar) hitting /api/cron/social-graphics weekly
Holiday template has seasonally-appropriate assets (snowflakes Dec, flowers Spring) selected by current month

stories.title: Social Graphic Export & Social Publishing
stories.description: Implement server-side rendering of social proof graphics to PNG/JPG/WebP, 2x retina export, direct social media publishing, and scheduled posts.
acceptance_criteria: Export button in editor renders current canvas to PNG, JPG, or WebP format (selectable)
Server-side rendering via POST /api/dashboard/social-graphics/:id/render endpoint
Rendering uses Puppeteer/Playwright on server to screenshot the canvas HTML at exact canvas dimensions
2x retina export option: renders at 2x canvas dimensions for high-DPI displays
Rendered image uploaded to Supabase Storage and URL stored in social_proof_graphics.render_url
render_status tracks: pending → rendering → complete (with URL) or failed (with error)
Download button provides rendered image file download with configurable filename
Direct publish to social platforms: Facebook, LinkedIn, Twitter/X via existing social_connections OAuth tokens
Publish dialog: select platform(s), add/edit caption, preview post, publish button
AI caption generation: button generates a social media caption from the review text using OpenAI (consistent with existing AI patterns in src/lib/ai/)
AI caption respects platform character limits (Twitter 280, LinkedIn 3000, Facebook 63206)
Scheduled posts: select date/time, platform(s), caption → stored and executed via cron
Post history: list of published/scheduled posts with platform, date, status, link to post
Error handling: graceful failures with retry option for rendering and publishing

key_decisions: Puppeteer/Playwright for server-side rendering because canvas elements are HTML/CSS (not <canvas>)
Rendering runs in a serverless function with 30s timeout; complex graphics may need optimization
AI captions use same OpenAI integration pattern as src/lib/ai/response-suggestions.ts
Social publishing reuses existing social_connections OAuth infrastructure for token management

stories.title: SEO Dashboard (Structured Data Validation & Rich Snippet Tracking)
stories.description: Build an SEO dashboard for monitoring structured data health, validating JSON-LD output, and tracking Rich Snippet appearances in search results.
acceptance_criteria: SEO dashboard page at /dashboard/widgets/seo or tab within widget analytics
Per-widget structured data preview showing rendered JSON-LD with syntax highlighting
Validation panel runs JSON-LD through schema.org validation rules and shows errors/warnings
Validation checks: required fields present, rating values in range, valid schema type, proper @context
Quick-fix suggestions for common validation issues with one-click apply
Rich Snippet status tracker: shows which widgets have structured data enabled, last validated date, validation status (valid, warnings, errors)
Google Search Console integration guidance: instructions for submitting URLs with structured data
Bulk validation: validate all active widgets at once with summary report
Export validation report as CSV or PDF
Schema type recommendation engine: suggests optimal schema type based on entity type and industry
Preview of how Rich Snippet would appear in Google search results (simulated SERP preview)
Alert system: notification when a widget's structured data becomes invalid (e.g., after config change)

key_decisions: Validation runs client-side against a local schema.org rules subset (not external API) for speed
SERP preview is a static HTML mockup matching Google's current result card layout
No actual Google Search Console API integration in this story (guidance only); future story could add it
Validation re-runs on every widget config save to keep status current

stories.title: Widget Version History & Rollback
stories.description: Implement version history tracking for widget configurations with diff view and one-click rollback to any previous version.
acceptance_criteria: Every widget config save increments the version number and creates a snapshot in widget_config_versions (or uses parent_widget_id chain)
Version history panel in Widget Builder showing: version number, date, changed_by user, change summary (auto-generated diff description)
Diff view between any two versions showing changed fields with before/after values
Config JSONB diff highlights: added fields (green), removed fields (red), changed values (yellow)
Rollback action: select a previous version → confirm dialog → restores that config as a new version (non-destructive, creates v+1 with old config)
Maximum 50 versions retained per widget; oldest versions auto-pruned
Version comparison: side-by-side preview of two versions showing visual widget output differences
Version metadata: stores who made the change and optional change note/description
API: GET /api/dashboard/widgets/:id/versions returns version history
API: POST /api/dashboard/widgets/:id/rollback/:version restores a specific version
Version history accessible from Widget Builder sidebar
Rollback preserves analytics data (events still reference the same widget_id)

key_decisions: Versions stored as complete config snapshots (not deltas) for simplicity and fast rollback
50-version limit with auto-pruning prevents unbounded storage growth
Rollback is always forward (creates new version) to maintain audit trail
JSONB diff algorithm: deep object comparison with path-based change tracking

stories.title: Multi-Language Support (English, Spanish)
stories.description: Add multi-language support to widgets for English and Spanish, including all UI strings, review content display, and builder language selection.
acceptance_criteria: Widget config supports config.content.language field: 'en' | 'es' (default 'en')
All widget UI strings (headers, buttons, labels, dates, empty states) translated to Spanish
Translation strings stored in locale files: en.json and es.json
embed.js includes both locale files (< 2KB additional bundle size)
Date formatting respects locale (e.g., '15 de enero de 2026' for Spanish)
Relative dates localized: 'hace 2 días' instead of '2 days ago'
Star rating ARIA labels localized: 'Calificado X de 5' for Spanish
CTA button default text localized: 'Escribir una reseña' for Spanish
Review text remains in its original language (not auto-translated)
Widget Builder shows language dropdown in Content settings tab
Preview updates immediately when language changes
Compliance disclaimers have separate Spanish versions stored in config
NMLS text remains in English (regulatory requirement — no translation)
Architecture supports future language additions without embed.js rebuild (locale files loaded dynamically for non-en/es)

key_decisions: en and es bundled inline to avoid extra network requests; future languages loaded dynamically via API
Simple key-value translation map (no ICU MessageFormat) to keep bundle small
Date formatting uses Intl.DateTimeFormat and Intl.RelativeTimeFormat (native browser APIs, no library)
NMLS text explicitly excluded from translation per regulatory guidance

stories.title: Google Tag Manager Template & Platform Integration Guides
stories.description: Create a Google Tag Manager custom template for widget embedding and comprehensive integration guides for Webflow, Squarespace, and other platforms.
acceptance_criteria: Google Tag Manager custom template published: allows adding RepWell widget via GTM UI with widget_id input field
GTM template injects embed.js script and widget div into page via Custom HTML tag
GTM template supports trigger configuration: page load, DOM ready, custom event
GTM template tested and validated in GTM preview mode

Webflow integration guide: step-by-step with screenshots for adding embed code via Custom Code block and Collection-level embedding
Squarespace integration guide: instructions for Code Injection (header/footer) and Code Block embedding
Shopify integration guide: instructions for theme.liquid and section embedding
General iframe embed guide for platforms that restrict script tags
Integration guides accessible from Widget Builder embed code panel as contextual help links
Each guide includes troubleshooting section for common issues (CSP headers, script blocking, styling conflicts)
Dashboard page at /dashboard/widgets/integrations listing all available integration methods with guides

key_decisions: GTM template uses Custom HTML tag type (not custom JavaScript variable) for simplicity
Guides rendered as React components (not markdown) for interactive code snippets with copy buttons
Iframe embed fallback provided for platforms with strict CSP that block third-party scripts
Guides include platform-specific screenshots stored in public/images/guides/

stories.title: Advanced Customization: Custom CSS Injection & JS Hooks
stories.description: Enable power users to inject custom CSS into widgets and register JavaScript hooks for advanced behavior customization, with safety guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: Widget config supports config.advanced.customCSS field: string of CSS rules injected inside Shadow DOM <style> tag
Custom CSS editor in Widget Builder: code editor with syntax highlighting (using Monaco or CodeMirror lightweight variant)
CSS validation: warns on potentially harmful rules (position:fixed, z-index >99999, pointer-events:none on entire widget)
CSS character limit: max 5000 characters to prevent abuse
Custom CSS preview updates live in widget preview as user types (debounced 300ms)
JavaScript hooks API: RepWell.on(widgetId, event, callback) for subscribing to widget events externally
Supported JS hook events: 'ready', 'review-loaded', 'review-clicked', 'cta-clicked', 'error'
Hook callbacks receive event data object with relevant context (review data, widget config, etc.)
RepWell.configure(widgetId, overrides) method for runtime config overrides from host page JS
Runtime overrides restricted to safe fields (theme colors, content toggles) — cannot override widget_id, organization_id, or security fields
Documentation page for JS hooks API with code examples
Custom CSS and JS hooks work correctly with all 9 widget types
Security: custom CSS sanitized to prevent data: URL injection and @import of external stylesheets

key_decisions: Custom CSS injected as final <style> block in Shadow DOM to ensure it overrides default styles
CSS sanitization strips @import, url(data:), expression(), and javascript: schemes
JS hooks use a pub/sub pattern within the RepWell global namespace, not CustomEvent on document
Runtime config overrides are validated against a whitelist of safe fields before applying
Code editor uses lightweight CodeMirror 6 (tree-shakeable) not full Monaco to keep bundle reasonable

stories.title: Widget E2E Tests & Performance Benchmarks
stories.description: Comprehensive end-to-end tests for all widget types, embed flow, builder UI, and performance benchmarks validating bundle size and rendering speed requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Playwright E2E tests for widget builder: create widget flow for each of the 9 types, configure settings, save, verify embed code generated
Playwright E2E test for embed flow: load page with embed script + widget div, verify widget renders with correct data, verify Shadow DOM encapsulation
E2E test for multiple widgets on single page: verify independent rendering and no interference
E2E test for domain restriction: widget blocked on unauthorized domain, allowed on authorized domain
E2E test for widget analytics: verify impression event fires on widget visible, click event on interaction
E2E test for carousel: verify auto-play, navigation, transition animations
E2E test for social proof banner: verify trigger conditions (scroll, time, exit-intent), dismiss persistence
E2E test for video testimonial: verify play, progress events, transcript sync
Performance benchmark: embed.js bundle size assertion (< 15KB gzipped) in CI pipeline
Performance benchmark: Lighthouse test on page with widget, assert impact < 5 points
Performance benchmark: First paint < 100ms, full render < 300ms measured via Performance API marks
Performance benchmark: CLS measurement asserts 0 contribution from widget
Performance benchmark: Memory profiling with 5 widgets asserts < 2MB total heap increase
All tests run in CI via GitHub Actions on PR creation and merge to main

key_decisions: Playwright for E2E tests (consistent with existing test setup)
Performance benchmarks use Playwright's CDP integration for Lighthouse and Performance API access
Bundle size check uses a simple script that builds and checks gzip size, fails CI if exceeded
Memory profiling uses Chrome DevTools Protocol heap snapshot via Playwright
Test fixtures include seeded widget configs and review data
